title: Fleet provisioning: post stage progress + failure summaries to Slack (#eng-infra)
author: Gabe Wilson
description: Adds Slack progress updates for Dedicated pool provisioning runs into #eng-infra, using the structured provisioning events emitted by the fleet provisioner. Motivation: during the staging + customer pilot we had long gaps where operators/SREs didn’t know whether a run was making progress vs stuck, and failures required digging through logs to reconstruct what happened. This PR posts a single “run header” message per provisioning run and then posts stage transition updates as thread replies (stage start/finish/fail), including per-stage duration and a compact failure summary when applicable. It also includes guardrails to avoid noise (dedupe + rate limit), plus explicit links to dashboards/runbooks/Linear. Behavior overview: 1) On run start: post header with pool_id, customer (if present), region, sku, run_id/correlation_id, and a link to the control plane run status endpoint. 2) On stage finish: post a thread reply: StageName ✅ duration=MM:SS (includes previous stage duration and overall elapsed). 3) On stage failure: post a thread reply: StageName ❌ duration=MM:SS reason=<normalized error category> + top-level error message (truncated) + links (logs query + runbook section). 4) On run completion: post final summary (overall time-to-ready, retries, and whether break-glass was used). Implementation notes: - New notifier module in fleet-provisioner subscribes to provisioning events and formats Slack Block Kit messages (kept minimal; avoids large payloads). - Uses the existing internal Slack app token stored in secrets manager; channel is configurable per env (defaults to #eng-infra in prod; #eng-infra-staging in staging). - Dedupe key is (run_id, stage, transition) to prevent duplicate posts when we retry event delivery. - Soft rate limit to max 1 message / 2s per run; bursts are buffered to avoid Slack API 429s during fast stage transitions in small pools. - Failure categorization reuses the error taxonomy introduced in telemetry work so alerting and Slack summaries match (dns_tls, gpu_health, quota, terraform_apply, helm_values, perf_canary, unknown). - Adds an opt-out feature flag (PROVISIONING_SLACK_NOTIFICATIONS=0) for staged rollout and emergency mute. Testing: unit tests for formatting + truncation + dedupe; integration test with a stub Slack API server to validate thread behavior and retry on 429. Rollout plan: enable in staging first, verify noise levels for 2–3 runs, then enable in prod for internal pools only; customer pools after SRE signoff. Screenshots and example payloads are in the test fixture output (see changed files).
commits: fleet-provisioner: provisioning event subscriber -> Slack thread updates
formatting: stage duration + normalized error category in message payloads
dedupe/rate-limit: prevent duplicate Slack posts on retry
tests: message formatting + slack stub integration test
docs: operator notes + env vars for provisioning Slack notifications
conversation: Vanessa Ortiz (review): Thread-per-run is the right shape. Two concerns: (1) can we guarantee we don’t spam #eng-infra on retries? We saw duplicate updates last week. (2) please include pool name/customer label in the header because the pool_id alone is hard to scan. Gabe Wilson (author): Added a dedupe cache keyed by (run_id, stage, transition) with a 7d TTL and also wired it to the persisted event id when available. Also updated header to include pool_name and customer_slug when present; otherwise displays “customer: (unknown)”. Rafael Mendes (review): Please make sure failure messages are actionable: link to the exact runbook section, not just the runbook root, and include the control-plane run status link for quick triage. Also, don’t post per-node GPU failures; we only need the aggregated category and a pointer. Gabe Wilson (author): Updated failure payload to include runbook anchors (e.g., dedicated-pool-provisioning-runbook#gpu-health-check, #dns-tls). Also changed gpu_health failures to summarize count of failed nodes and first error sample, with a link to the logs query; no per-node spam. Allison Grant (review): Watch out for PII in Slack: do we ever include customer-provided strings? Also add a safeguard for Slack 429s; we’ll hit rate limits during fast transitions in small pools. Gabe Wilson (author): Added a sanitizer: customer_slug is from our CRM normalization and pool_name is validated (alnum + dash/underscore) before posting; any unexpected characters get stripped and we fall back to pool_id only. Implemented backoff + buffering on 429 and a per-run soft rate limit (1 msg/2s). Ethan Park (review): Nit: put notifications behind the same provisioning feature flag so we can disable quickly. Also, can we post to #eng-infra-staging by default in staging? Gabe Wilson (author): Done. Added PROVISIONING_SLACK_NOTIFICATIONS and default channel routing by env (staging -> #eng-infra-staging, prod -> #eng-infra). Final approval: Vanessa Ortiz: LGTM after dedupe + header update. Rafael Mendes: Approved, ship to staging first. Allison Grant: Approved; please monitor message volume for a day and report back in ENG-2758.
checks: CI: build-and-unit-tests (pass); lint (pass); typecheck (pass); integration-tests (pass); security-scan (pass). Note: integration-tests initially failed once due to a flaky timing assertion in the Slack stub server; rerun passed after adjusting the test to wait for the retry/backoff window.
release_notes: Operator visibility: provisioning runs now post stage-by-stage progress and failure summaries to Slack (#eng-infra) with durations and links to dashboards/runbooks; gated behind PROVISIONING_SLACK_NOTIFICATIONS for staged rollout.
